newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish trader sells 14,000 T wheat to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkish trader sells 14,000 T wheat to Iraq.

text.p: Turkish commodities trading and port company Toros said on Wednesday it was selling Iraq 14,000 tonnes of imported wheat under a U.N. aid programme for Iraq.
"The wheat is heading to Iraq these days," said company vice-President Yavuz Kuran.

"It is being sent with private trucks with a daily transport of 700 tonnes from our port terminal (on the Mediterranean)," he told Reuters on the sidelines of an international grains conference in this southern Turkish town.
He said the sale was under the U.N. humanitarian aid programme for Iraq which has been in place since a trade embargo was imposed on Baghdad after its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
Traders attending the conference said the sale was the first of any foodstuff in the past two months to Iraq.

Humanitarian trade with Iraq has come to a standstill in the past two months on hopes that implementation of a U.N. plan to let Iraq sell oil worth $2 billion to buy food and medicine would revive trade with this country.
But the plan was suspended by the United Nations earlier this month when Iraqi forces attacked the Kurds in the country's north, leading to U.S. missile attacks on military targets in southern Iraq.
